title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): to a graph G with half-edge set Â, Grothendieck attaches a real torus P_G = ∏_{a∈Â} T_a. Each T_a is a U(1)-torsor, i.e. a circle. Inside each T_a sits a two-point set ε_a, an antipodal pair defined combinatorially from the graph. So Sε_G = ∏ ε_a is a set of 2^{|Â|} points of the torus. S_0T_G is the fundamental groupoid of P_G restricted to these 2^{|Â|} points (the base points). It maps to the Teichmüller-type groupoid ST_{G⇄} through the simply connected cell μ°×SP_G → PM.

This page gives an explicit presentation of S_0T_G.

(i) Sign-indexed presentation.
- The sign group {±1}^Â acts on Sε_G: α·ξ flips the coordinates where α_a = −1.
- For each sign vector α and base point ξ, the path u_{α,ξ}(t)_a is constant where α_a = +1. Where α_a = −1 it is exp(πit)ξ_a, a positive half-turn. It runs from ξ to αξ.
- The fundamental group at each object is Z^Â (full turns). Composition rule: u_{β,αξ} ∘ u_{α,ξ} = u_{αβ,ξ} + n(α,β). Here n(α,β)_a = 1 exactly when α_a = β_a = −1, since two half-turns make one full turn; otherwise it is 0.
- n is the 'carry' 2-cocycle of the extension 0 → Z^Â → (½Z)^Â → (Z/2)^Â → 0.
- Equivalently, S_0T_G is the action groupoid of the lattice (½Z)^Â ≅ Z^Â (generated by half-turns), acting on Sε_G through reduction mod 2. Its vertex groups are 2·(½Z)^Â = Z^Â.

(ii) Elementary presentation.
- Generators: u_{a,ξ}: ξ → σ_aξ, a half-turn in coordinate a alone.
- Relations (1): for a ≠ b, the squares u_{b,σ_aξ} u_{a,ξ} = u_{a,σ_bξ} u_{b,ξ} commute.
- Relations (2), on the next page: the full turns v^a_ξ = u_{a,σ_aξ} u_{a,ξ} commute pairwise.
- Topologically, this is the fundamental groupoid of the 2-skeleton of the product cubulation of (S^1)^Â. Each circle carries 2 vertices and 2 edges, the 2-cells are the squares, and the vertex set is Sε_G.

Purpose: a discrete, combinatorial model of the twist (Dehn-twist torus) part of the Teichmüller groupoid near a maximally degenerate stable curve. It uses 2^{|Â|} 'tangential' base points instead of one. The next page passes to the non-'S' version _0T_G and draws a commutative square comparing S_0T_G → ST_G with _0T_G → T_G.
errors: The lower-right corner of square (1) is written 'σ_{ab}'; it should be σ_aσ_bξ (= σ_bσ_aξ).

Relation (2), that the full turns v^a_ξ commute, is redundant given the squares (1) for all a ≠ b. By the 2-skeleton/cubulation argument, (1) already forces all the u's to commute up to base change, so vertex groups are abelian. Harmless, but not needed.
The opening phrase 'engendré par les objets de Sε_G' really means the object set is Sε_G and generators are u_{α,ξ}. That is wording, not a mathematical error.

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of a torus restricted to the finite set of 2^n 'antipodal' base points, presented by half-turn generators and a carry cocycle n(α,β)
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid on a set of base points; action groupoid (½Z)^n ⋉ (Z/2)^n; carry 2-cocycle of Z → ½Z → Z/2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Brown's fundamental groupoid on a set of base points, 1967)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme advocates groupoids with several base points but contains no such explicit presentation

ideas.what: Presentation by elementary half-twist generators u_{a,ξ} with commuting-square relations
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid of the 2-skeleton of the product cubulation of (S^1)^n

ideas.what: Using the 2^{|edges|} sign/orientation choices at a maximally degenerate curve as base points, with half-twists as generators of the twist part of the Teichmüller groupoid
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points at maximal degenerations; half-twists in the Lego-Teichmüller groupoid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Moore–Seiberg (1989); Bakalov–Kirillov (2000); Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000); Nakamura (tangential base points)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches the Teichmüller tower and base points at maximal degeneration only in outline

missed.claim: This is an early (around 1978+) explicit combinatorial model of the 'twist torus' local piece of the Teichmüller groupoid. It uses 2^{|Â|} discrete base points and half-turn generators, with a carry cocycle n(α,β) recording that two half-twists make a Dehn twist. It anticipates the half-twist/twist generators of the later Lego-Teichmüller groupoids, but the content of this page itself is standard.
missed.quote: u_{α,ξ}(t)_a = (exp(πit))ξ_a si α_a = −1 ... n(α,β)_a = 1 sinon (i.e. α_a = β_a = −1)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents that Grothendieck worked with multi-base-point groupoids and half-twists before the Moore–Seiberg and Bakalov–Kirillov formalisms. It is not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a correct but routine presentation of the fundamental groupoid of a torus at antipodal base points. Its interest is only as an early historical trace of the Teichmüller-groupoid program.
transcription_corrections: The corner of diagram (1) 'σ_{ab}' should be read as σ_aσ_bξ (σ_{ab}ξ).
The relation line should read: u_{β,ξ'} ∘ u_{α,ξ} = u_{αβ,ξ} + n(α,β), using the Z^Â-structure, i.e. the composite equals u_{αβ,ξ} translated by n(α,β).
'Indépendamment, pour l'utiliser' is likely 'Indépendamment, sans l'utiliser', i.e. an alternative presentation not using the Z^Â-structure.
